sections.label: Comfort walking streets alone at night
sections.summary: 97% of people said they would be comfortable walking the streets of Singapore alone at night.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In stark contrast, when we ask people how they feel about walking the streets of Singapore alone at night, 97% said that they would be comfortable to do so.

sections.label: Harmful online content well-being consequences
sections.summary: The prevalence of harmful online content on these services can have negative serious consequences on society's physical, emotional and mental well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Because of this, the prevalence of harmful online content on these services can have negative serious consequences on the physical, emotional and mental well-being of society.

sections.label: Online content damage and foreign platforms
sections.summary: Online content can inflict serious damage if laws fall short, and entities controlling the biggest online communication services accessible in Singapore operate outside Singapore and outside the Broadcasting Act's legal remit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In the same way, we must recognise that online content can inflict serious damage on our people and communities, if our laws fall short.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We must have the ability to deal with harmful online content accessible to Singapore users, regardless of where the content is hosted or initiated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The entities controlling the biggest and most popular online communication services (OCSs) or platforms accessible in Singapore all operate outside of Singapore and fall outside the legal remit of the Broadcasting Act today.

sections.label: MCI public consultation responses
sections.summary: In July and August this year, MCI conducted a public consultation and engagements on proposals to combat harmful online content and received more than 600 responses.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In July and August this year, MCI conducted a public consultation and series of engagements on our proposals to combat harmful online content and received more than 600 responses.

sections.label: Bill regulating online communication services
sections.summary: If passed, the Bill will create a new part in the Broadcasting Act to regulate online communication services, which are electronic services enabling users to access or communicate content via the Internet.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If passed by Parliament, this Bill will create a new part in the Broadcasting Act to regulate "online communication service", which are electronic services that enable users to access or communicate content via the Internet.

sections.label: Users experiencing harmful content online
sections.summary: About three in five users from MCI's June 2022 survey experienced harmful content online using social media platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Well, because three in five users or thereabout from MCI's June 2022 survey experienced harmful content online using social media platforms.

sections.label: Designating online communication services
sections.summary: Sections 45K and 45L let IMDA designate OCSs with significant reach or impact and require safety measures via Codes of Practice.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Under sections 45K and 45L of the proposed Bill, IMDA will be able to designate OCSs with significant reach or impact in Singapore, and require them, via the Codes of Practice, to put in place measures to keep Singapore users safe.

sections.label: Key outcomes for designated services
sections.summary: Designated social media services must minimise Singapore users' exposure to harmful content and give users safety management tools.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The designated social media services will be expected to meet the key outcomes as follows: First, minimise Singapore users' exposure to harmful content and empower users with tools to manage their own safety.

sections.label: IMDA as online firefighter
sections.summary: New section 45H lets IMDA direct any social media service to disable Singapore users' access to egregious content and stop its transmission.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If Parliament agrees, the new section 45H proposed by this Bill will allow IMDA to act as an "online firefighter", to direct any social media service to disable Singapore users' access to egregious content and stop the egregious content from being transmitted to Singapore users via other channels or accounts.

sections.label: Definition of egregious content
sections.summary: New section 45D defines egregious content to include terrorism, suicide, self-harm, violence, child sexual exploitation, public health risk and racial or religious harm.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The new section 45D proposed by the Bill defines "egregious content" to include content advocating terrorism, suicide and self-harm, violence including sexual violence, child sexual exploitation, content posing public health risk and content likely to undermine racial and religious harmony.

sections.label: Compliance and penalties for services
sections.summary: Section 45M requires designated services to comply with Codes of Practice, with penalties and rectification directions under section 45N for non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The new section 45M proposed in the Bill requires designated services to take all reasonably practicable steps to comply with an applicable Code of Practice.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If they do not, IMDA can take regulatory action under the proposed section 45N to issue (a) a financial penalty; or (b) a rectification direction requiring the service to remedy the failure to comply with the Code of Practice.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Non-compliance with a rectification direction will be a criminal offence, punishable with a fine.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For egregious content, non-compliance with a direction by IMDA will also be a criminal offence, punishable by a fine.

sections.label: S.U.R.E. engagement numbers
sections.summary: Since its 2013 launch, S.U.R.E. has conducted over 6 million physical and digital engagements.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Since its launch in 2013, S.U.R.E. has conducted over 6 million physical and digital engagements.

sections.label: Self-harm content harms young people
sections.summary: Molly ended her life after being badly affected by thousands of self-harm and suicide contents, and such content flooding cyberspace could adversely affect many, especially the young, and risk social cohesion.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Badly affected by the thousands of contents about self-harm and suicide, young Molly ended her short life.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: If we allow such content to flood our cyberspace, many people, especially our young, would be adversely affected; and the social cohesion that we built preciously over the years may also be at risk.

sections.label: Accountability and community support for online safety
sections.summary: The speaker says OCSs must be held accountable for Singapore users' safety and asks Members to support the Bill to improve online safety together.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: To ensure that safety is upheld for Singapore users, we need OCSs to be held accountable.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Equally, we need the support of everyone in the community to keep each other safe online.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: I appeal to Members to support this Bill so that we can together improve online safety.

sections.label: Online Safety (Miscellaneous Amendment) Bill purpose
sections.summary: The Bill builds on existing laws to recognise that online happenings can have real physical-world impact and that actions must address safety and well-being.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The Online Safety (Miscellaneous Amendment) Bill builds on some of our existing laws to further recognise that happenings online can have a real impact in the physical world and actions must be taken to address issues concerning the safety and well-being of our people.

sections.label: Question on whitelist determination
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Ministry determines which OCS providers make it into the whitelist.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, I have the following questions to ask about the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to ask: how does the Ministry determine which OCS providers make it into the whitelist?

sections.label: Question on egregious content threshold
sections.summary: The speaker asks who will assess and decide what crosses the threshold to qualify as egregious content, given the Ministry's broad list.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Thirdly, while the Ministry has a broad list of what constitutes egregious content, such as content that advocates or instructs on suicide, self-harm, violence, child sexual exploitation, public health risk, racial and religious disharmony and terrorism, who and how will this assessment and decision be made on what actually crosses the threshold to qualify as egregious?

sections.label: Questions on metaverse, Web 3.0 protection
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Bill protects users from similar metaverse harms and whether legislation and enforcement will keep pace with Web 3.0, and hopes the Ministry shares more on engaging industry and community stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Though these reports were specific to Meta's metaverse platform, it is not difficult to imagine similar incidents happening on other metaverse platforms, especially if the different metaverse universes start to connect with one another.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, how will the Bill, in its current form, be able to protect users from such online harms?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In addition, as we look to a possible future of Web 3.0, where data and control become decentralised, going just after a couple of OCS providers operating in the Web 2.0 world may not be effective enough.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, we will need to ensure that our legislation and enforcement capabilities are updated in a timely manner, so that while we do not want to be over-prescriptive, we are also not too big a step behind these technological developments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, I hope the Ministry can also share more about what is being done to continually engage industry players and community stakeholders so that our legislation and Codes of Practice not only have teeth but will bite where it matters.

sections.label: Age verification checks question
sections.summary: Asks how content providers will be required to perform age verification checks in practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can I ask the Minister: how will content providers be required to perform age verification checks in practice?

sections.label: Default network-level filtering proposal
sections.summary: Argues parental sign-up friction leaves children vulnerable and proposes default remote filtering by Internet service providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This additional friction will deter many parents from signing up, leaving young children vulnerable to accessing harmful content without their parents' knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It would be better for Internet service providers to block harmful content at the network level by default, rather than expect parents to set up complicated filtering software on their children's devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This remote filtering should be activated by default for all new mobile and broadband subscriptions and offered for free for all subscribers.

sections.label: Offence for non-compliance with IMDA
sections.summary: States that failing to comply with IMDA directions could be an offence punishable by a fine on conviction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under this Bill, failure to comply with the directions from IMDA could be an offence punishable by a fine on conviction.

sections.label: Annual reports to IMDA
sections.summary: States the Code of Practice will require social media services to submit annual reports to IMDA on Singapore users' experiences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Code of Practice will require social media services to submit annual reports to IMDA to reflect Singapore users' experiences on the service, including the actions that they have taken on user reports.

sections.label: Australia comparison and gaming questions
sections.summary: Contrasts Australia's Online Safety Act complaints system and asks about regulation of online gaming and non-consensual intimate images.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In contrast, Australia's Online Safety Act requires platforms to provide a clear and easily accessible complaints system for end-users to submit complaints or requests to remove certain material and the platforms must respond to the complainant within 48 hours, failing which the end-user may contact the eSafety Commissioner, who has the power to investigate the complaint.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share to what extent this Bill and the Code of Practice will regulate online gaming?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Will the non-consensual sharing of intimate images be covered in this Bill?

sections.label: Defence Guild SG pro bono initiative
sections.summary: Describes Defence Guild SG, a group of over 20 lawyers providing pro bono help to victims of online abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In June 2021, I started an initiative called Defence Guild SG, a collaborative group of lawyers providing pro bono assistance to victims of online abuse or harms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We now have over 20 lawyers who volunteer pro bono to assist or advise victims who face sexual harassment or online harms.

sections.label: Online harms legal help suggestions
sections.summary: A survey found almost 57% do not know legal redress for online harms, prompting three suggestions on legal advice, reporting and awareness campaigns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding all of the efforts, according to a recent survey, almost 57% do not know what are the legal redress or help that they can get when faced with online harms personally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this regard, I have three suggestions: first, to provide legal pro bono advice under the Legal Aid Bureau for individuals facing online harms, much like what Defence Guild SG is doing for victims currently; second, to standardise the ease of reporting of online harms across all platforms; third, to seek platform and broadcasting service providers to be included in public awareness campaigns on eradicating online harms.

sections.label: Bill places responsibility on service providers
sections.summary: The Bill places responsibility on service providers to block harmful online content such as extremist content, violence and content affecting multiracial and multi-religious society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, this protection could not have come about without the partnership of those from the Government, individuals and technology companies or online service providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Therefore, this Bill places responsibility in the hands of service providers, to block online content that may cause harm, such as extremist content, violence and those that negatively impact our multiracial and multi-religious society.

sections.label: Team budget of AUD$3 million
sections.summary: The team has a budget of around AUD$3 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The team has a budget of around AUD$3 million.

sections.label: New clause 45E offence
sections.summary: New clause 45E makes it an offence of not stopping egregious content on an OCS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In particular, the new clause 45E makes it an offence of not stopping egregious content on an OCS.

sections.label: Germany's 24-hour takedown requirement
sections.summary: Germany's similar law provides for a 24-hour requirement for takedown.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For example, Germany's similar law provides for a 24-hour requirement for takedown.

sections.label: Estimated period for direction or order
sections.summary: A request asks the Minister to clarify the estimated period envisaged for a typical direction or order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Alternatively, perhaps, Minister can clarify what is the estimated period that is envisaged for a typical direction or order?

sections.label: POHA use against individual
sections.summary: The Protection from Harassment Act was used by MINDEF against an individual, and the legitimacy of this was disputed in a Court of Appeals ruling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Members will recall how the Protection from Harassment Act (POHA) was used by the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) to take action against an individual, the legitimacy of which was disputed in a subsequent ruling of the Court of Appeals.

sections.label: Egregious content definition gaps
sections.summary: The speaker says the Bill's definition of egregious content does not adequately deal with revenge porn or unwanted sharing of intimate images, and cyberbullying.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In particular, I think that the definition of egregious content given here in the Bill does not adequately deal with the following two categories: firstly, revenge porn or unwanted sharing of intimate images; and secondly, cyberbullying.

sections.label: PISA bullying statistics Singapore
sections.summary: A 2019 PISA study found 26% of Singaporean students reported being bullied at least a few times a month, against an OECD average of 23%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A 2019 Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) study found that 26% of Singaporean students reported being bullied at least a few times a month, compared to an Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) average of 23%.

sections.label: Megan Meier cyberbullying suicide
sections.summary: In America, Megan Meier committed suicide three weeks before her 14th birthday, attributed to cyberbullying on MySpace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In America, a girl called Megan Meier committed suicide three weeks before her 14th birthday and her suicide was attributed to cyberbullying on the social networking site MySpace.

sections.label: Cyberbullying suicide thoughts study
sections.summary: A US National Institute of Health study found child participants who experienced cyberbullying were over four times as likely to report suicidal thoughts and attempts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A large-scale National Institute of Health study in the United States (US) found that "the child participants who experienced cyberbullying were more than four times as likely to report thoughts of suicide and attempts as those who did not." I think this subject of youth mental health, in the context of social media, has been the subject of much public discussion and much research and rightly so, as many experts are tending towards a view that there is a connection between the very extensive social media usage that we are seeing among young people, and the kinds of mental health issues that are coming to the fore.

sections.label: Anti-bullying education and ambassadors
sections.summary: The speaker calls for targeted school education on bystander responsibility and suggests enlisting students who stood up to bullying as anti-bullying ambassadors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In particular, we need targeted education in primary and secondary schools that helps students to recognise that as bystanders, they have an important responsibility to step in and stop bullying, or at least to not cooperate and to flag out potential issues to teachers or others in authority positions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Encouragingly, the PISA study I cited earlier found that 94% of Singaporean students agreed that it is a good thing to help students who cannot defend themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For this kind of education to work better, I am wondering if we can enlist students who have stood up to bullying, either as victims or bystanders, to be anti-bullying ambassadors who give talks in schools as to what they experienced, what they did, how they coped and also, when and how to bring the authorities in, as opposed to necessarily escalating every single situation to people in authority.

sections.label: Loot boxes and gambling
sections.summary: Belgium banned real-money loot boxes, the UK NHS called for an industry ban, and a UK study found loot boxes psychologically akin to gambling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Belgium has banned loot boxes purchased using real money.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: The UK National Health Services (NHS) have also called for the industry to ban loot boxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: A report produced by researchers at the universities of Plymouth and Wolverhampton in UK, as reported by the BBC in April 2021, found that loot boxes "are structurally and psychologically akin to gambling." According to the study in the UK, "Of the 93% of children who play video games, up to 40% opened loot boxes.

sections.label: Gambling harm to families
sections.summary: The speaker notes financial losses and social harm affect family members and welcomes the Gambling Regulatory Authority's August announcement on loot boxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: While it affects a small percentage of the population directly, the financial losses and social harm they generate can easily affect their family members and loved ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: I am glad to note that the Gambling Regulatory Authority announced in August this year that it is looking at loot boxes.

sections.label: Online harm legislation
sections.summary: The Government has taken proactive steps to mitigate online harm through legislation such as POFMA, FICA and POHA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government has, in recent years, taken proactive steps to mitigate the possibilities of online harm through legislation, such as online falsehoods (POFMA), foreign interference, hostile information campaigns (FICA) and online harassment (POHA).

sections.label: Social media lawsuit dismissed
sections.summary: Parents sued a social media platform and its parent company in May 2022 over harmful content, but a federal judge dismissed the lawsuit last month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The parents of one of the deceased children sued a social media platform and its parent company in May 2022 for exposing their child to harmful content, only for the lawsuit to be dismissed by a federal judge just last month, stating that the social media platform and its parent company were not responsible for the child’s death.

sections.label: Milk crate challenge injuries
sections.summary: The milk crate challenge encourages stacking and climbing crates, which could cause dislocations, cartilage damage or permanent spinal cord damage, prompting a question on where to draw the line.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: You might or might not be aware of the “milk crate challenge”, for example, which encourages the stacking and climbing of milk crates, which might not seem directly life-threatening – quite ridiculous, I know, but not directly life-threatening – but I would imagine that it could result in significant injuries, such as dislocations, cartilage damage and even potential permanent spinal cord damage, if one should fall badly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, my question to the Government is, where would we draw the line on what would be considered egregious and what would be permitted?

sections.label: Regulating egregious behaviour
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether egregious behaviour causing harm should be treated like egregious content and removed using platforms' algorithms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: After all, if we feel that egregious online content that causes harm should be regulated and controlled, then should not egregious behaviour that could result in harmful or negative outcomes also be treated the same way?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And if OCS have the sophisticated algorithms to identify cases of cyberbullying, then should we not work towards treating egregious behaviour like egregious content and possibly remove such material from the online platforms?

sections.label: User-friendly reporting portals
sections.summary: The passage states that effective reporting depends on user-friendly portals that make filing reports against questionable online content not too onerous, encouraging timely reporting and action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While there are different merits to having a centralised Government-administered portal versus a portal administered by the individual OCS, the crux to effective reporting would be that the portals are user-friendly and it would not be too onerous for users to file reports against questionable online content.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The ease of reporting will help to encourage timely reporting of such content and facilitate timely actions to regulate the content that could possibly cause online harm.

sections.label: Bill compels online content services
sections.summary: The passage states the Bill would compel many OCS, some criticised for algorithms driving behaviours, to play a significant part in keeping the online space safe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, I believe that this Bill is a step in the right direction as it would compel a large number of OCS, some of which have been criticised in the past for using algorithms to encourage and even drive certain behaviours, to also play their part, a significant part, in ensuring that the online space remains safe and conducive.

sections.label: Stakeholders must deal with challenge
sections.summary: The passage states that if this happens, it is good that Government, users and the OCS realise it and take steps to deal with the challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: If it does, then it is good that all stakeholders – Government, users and the OCS – sit up, realise this and take steps to deal with this challenge.

sections.label: Singaporeans experiencing online harms
sections.summary: The passage states nearly half of Singaporeans polled by the Sunlight Alliance for Action experienced online harms, and over 40% affected would not act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Nearly half of Singaporeans polled by the Sunlight Alliance for Action have personally experienced online harms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Yet, over 40% of people affected said that they would not take action, as they believe that nothing will come out of it.

sections.label: Gender-based online harms survey
sections.summary: The passage states the Sunlight Alliance for Action found 31% of respondents experienced or witnessed gender-based online harms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In fact, the Sunlight Alliance for Action found that 31% of respondents have experienced or witnessed gender-based online harms.

sections.label: AWARE image-based sexual abuse report
sections.summary: The passage states that in 2021 AWARE reported 70% of technology-facilitated sexual violence seen by its Sexual Assault Care Centre involved image-based sexual abuse.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In 2021, AWARE reported that 70% of technology-facilitated sexual violence seen by their Sexual Assault Care Centre involved image-based sexual abuse.

sections.label: Molly harmful social media content
sections.summary: Molly saved, liked or shared 16,300 pieces of content in six months, over 2,100 on suicide, depression and self-harm; the coroner ruled harmful social media contributed to her death.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the six months before her death, it was reported that Molly had saved, liked or shared 16,300 pieces of content on one platform alone, of which more than 2,100 in total, or 12 a day, were related to suicide, depression and self-harm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The coroner's inquest concluded recently, ruling that harmful social media content contributed to her death "in a more than minimal way".

sections.label: Regulating egregious online content
sections.summary: One section of the Bill lays out the state's enhanced ability to regulate online communication services found to display egregious content such as suicide, self-harm, violence and terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One section of the Bill lays out the state's enhanced ability to regulate online communication services if they are found to display egregious content, including content advocating suicide or self-harm, physical or sexual violence, terrorism and so on.

sections.label: Revenge photos of women online
sections.summary: Accounts exist of photos or videos of women, ex-girlfriends or ex-wives uploaded to social media for revenge or entertainment; the code of practice will cover only regulated OCS with significant reach or impact in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In addition, we have also read accounts of photos or videos of women, ex-girlfriends or ex-wives being uploaded on social media as a form of revenge or simply for entertainment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I understand that, presently, this code of practice will only cover regulated OCS that MCI has determined as having significant reach or impact in Singapore.

sections.label: Future digital amendments and consultation
sections.summary: Further amendments may be needed for new digital developments, and new regulations should be developed as a whole-of-society effort in consultation with the people and private sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Moving forward, it is likely that further amendments may be needed to respond to new developments in the digital space.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Any new regulations should be developed as a whole-of-society effort, in consultation with the people and private sectors, too.

sections.label: NUS Atheist Society Facebook post
sections.summary: In 2020 a Facebook post from the NUS Atheist Society, not affiliated with NUS, suggested the Bible and Quran as toilet paper alternatives; IMDA asked Facebook to disable access before it was taken down.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, in 2020, a Facebook post from the NUS Atheist Society, which is actually not affiliated with NUS, suggested using the Bible and Quran as alternatives in the event of a toilet paper shortage.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In that situation, IMDA stepped in to ask Facebook to disable access to the post before it was taken down.

sections.label: Christchurch attacker Facebook Live video
sections.summary: Using a GoPro camera, the attacker filmed himself on Facebook Live gunning down 51 people in two mosques; the video was viewed about 4,000 times before removal.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Using a GoPro camera, the attacker filmed himself using Facebook Live, gunning down 51 people in two mosques.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The video quickly went viral and was viewed about 4,000 times before it was removed.

sections.label: Online Safety Bill amendment welcomed
sections.summary: Speaker welcomes the proposed Online Safety Bill amendment and two significant requirements in the new measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: If we accept that our societies are governed by rules and laws that aim to maintain peace and harmony in our nation, then why should our online societies be absolved of such a need?

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is for this reason that I welcome the proposed amendment to the Online Safety Bill and, in particular, two significant requirements that were laid out in the new measures.

sections.label: Laws lack platform accountability
sections.summary: Existing laws like POHA do not hold social media platforms responsible for their action or lack thereof.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Even as Singapore has enacted legislation, such as the Protection from Harassment Act (POHA), to deal with such specific issues, these laws, currently, do not afford the capacity to hold social media platforms responsible regarding their action, or lack thereof, in dealing with such situations, especially where the platform wields significant control over the speed of the entire process and the final outcome.

sections.label: Platform report acknowledgement and outcome
sections.summary: The platform acknowledged the report immediately but four days later said it did not remove the account.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I received an acknowledgement note almost immediately from the platform saying that they had received the report and that they would use their community guidelines to review the account.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It was not until four days later that I received a note from the social media platform saying this, "We didn’t remove xxx account.

sections.label: Victim's ordeal and platform transparency
sections.summary: The victim received no updates, the post was removed late, the account stayed active, and transparency measures are welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Case closed." I note that at the time of the report, the account only had one post, which is the one the young lady had brought to my attention.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It was extremely troubling to know how helpless she, and even I, felt throughout this whole situation, as she received no update or communication from the social media platform regarding the case until the outcome was finalised, of which the post was removed only after an extended period of time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The account, however, remains active to this day, leaving the victim at the mercy of the anonymous user who could yet again subject the victim to another episode of doxxing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Social media platforms, you can do better, and we can do better for online safety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, heartening to see the call for greater transparency surrounding the decision-making processes of social media platforms, along with the tools, resources and enforcement options available to them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Yet, these measures do not fully grasp the emotional and mental turbulence that one experiences as a victim of online harm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The apparent lack of a human touch in the process of dealing with online harm by social media platforms reflects a certain degree of uncongeniality and coldness that does not work to protect and support victims in times of need, and perhaps should be re-evaluated.

sections.label: Enforcement challenges and Ministry plans
sections.summary: The question asks what enforcement challenges the Ministry envisages and how it intends to address them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What are the challenges envisaged by the Ministry with regard to enforcement of the law and how does the Ministry intend to address those challenges?

sections.label: Organising neighbourhood policing online
sections.summary: The question asks how the Ministry intends to organise neighbourhood policing against online harmful content.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How does the Ministry intend to organise such neighbourhood policing against online harmful content?

sections.label: Harmful content decision and overseas cases
sections.summary: Asks who decides what content is harmful and how the Government handles overseas-originating content not distributed by locally-licensed providers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Who will decide what content is harmful and thus will be subject to the legislation?

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How will the Government handle cases when the content originates from overseas and is not distributed by locally-licensed online communication service providers?

sections.label: Egregious content racial religious groups
sections.summary: Asks why the Bill's egregious content category covers racial and religious groups but not other demographic segments such as gender.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, the Bill defines one category of "egregious content" as content that is "likely to cause feelings of enmity, hatred, ill will or hostility against, or contempt for or ridicule of, different racial or religious groups in Singapore." Can the Minister share why this category does not include content that has a similar impact on other demographic segments, such as gender?

sections.label: AWARE sexual assault care centre clients
sections.summary: States that since 2016 AWARE's Sexual Assault Care Centre has supported 747 clients who experienced technology-facilitated sexual violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Since 2016, AWARE's Sexual Assault Care Centre has supported 747 clients who experienced technology-facilitated sexual violence.

sections.label: General duty of care compensation
sections.summary: Proposes creating a general duty of care on online communication providers to compensate individuals for harm from negligent management of harmful content.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, we can create a general duty of care on online communication providers to compensate individuals for harm they suffer due to the platform's negligence in managing harmful content.

sections.label: Police resources against end-users
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government will increase Police resources and training to assist victims and act swiftly against end-users posting harmful content.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To ensure sufficient deterrence against end-users, will the Government consider increasing resources and training for the Police to assist victims and take swift action against end-users who post harmful content?

sections.label: Broadcasting Act regulating online communication services
sections.summary: Describes the Bill's new Broadcasting Act part regulating Online Communication Services and asks whether messaging platforms like WhatsApp and Telegram are included.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces a new part to the Broadcasting Act to regulate Online Communication Services (OCS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, SMS will need to implement measures to limit local users' exposure to harmful content, thus forcing OCS to be more accountable to users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As there are many forms of social media, it would be good if the Ministry can clarify if messaging platforms, such as WhatsApp, Telegram, WeChat and Kakao Talk would be considered as SMS.

sections.label: Strategy games and future gaming legislation
sections.summary: The speaker agrees technology changes rapidly and says legislation on gaming can be planned for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are many genres of games that focus on strategy, desirable values and are productive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I agree with the Minister that the Internet and technology are changing rapidly and as we debate about the Online Safety Bill in the context of SMS today, we can plan for legislation on gaming in the future.

sections.label: Timeliness of Online Safety Bill measures
sections.summary: The speaker says the Bill's measures are timely because online communication service providers failed to self-regulate and remove harmful content.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The proposed measures under this Bill are, therefore, timely, as it will require online communication service (OCS) providers to be regulated and to remove harmful online content when asked to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Actually, I would argue that legislation has become necessary because the OCS providers have failed to properly self-regulate and remove harmful content from being posted on their platforms.

sections.label: VPN access and IMDA directive compliance speed
sections.summary: The speaker notes harmful content stays accessible via VPN subscription and asks how fast providers must comply with IMDA directives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In cases where an OCS provider disables access by Singapore users to a harmful content, it can still be easily accessible with a simple subscription to a VPN service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I would also like to ask how fast must an OCS provider comply with a directive issued by IMDA under this Bill.

sections.label: Mandatory age verification for new sign-ups
sections.summary: The speaker calls for mandatory age verification for all new sign-ups so new accounts comply with social media terms of use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: First, I call for mandatory age verification to be done for all new sign-ups, to ensure that new accounts being created comply with the terms of use set out by the social media service.

sections.label: Hypersexualised video game content and children
sections.summary: The speaker says games contain hypersexualised content, pornography and glorified violence, and hopes gaming regulation is reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: A key concern about the popularity of video games is that so much of the content is hypersexualised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Pornography is often embedded in these games and many games do glorify violence and sexual exploitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: For example, in the game "The Sims Online", a "cyber-brothel" was developed by a 17-year-old boy using the game alias "Evangeline" and customers paid sim-money for cybersex by the minute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: As such, many children unwittingly interact with strangers for the first time in these gaming platforms, raising significantly their online safety risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I really hope that the Ministry can include regulation of the online gaming space in the next review of the code of practice.

sections.label: IMDA directions on egregious content
sections.summary: The Bill adds a Broadcasting Act Part letting IMDA direct providers to block egregious content, and the speaker asks about foreign armed conflict videos.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: First, the principal amendment of the Bill is the addition of a new Part in the Broadcasting Act that will allow IMDA to issue directions to providers of online communication services to disable or block access to "egregious content". "Egregious content" is then defined in the new section 45D to include content that advocates or instructs on suicide, self-harm, child nudity and terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: First, does "content that advocates or instructs on violence or cruelty to, physical abuse of, or acts of torture or other infliction of serious physical harm on, human beings" catch videos that encourage Singaporeans to participate in a foreign armed conflict?

sections.label: Enforcing rules on foreign providers
sections.summary: Asks how the Ministry will enforce regulations against foreign service providers with no place of business or headquarters in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For such foreign service providers who do not have a place of business in Singapore or its headquarters (HQ), how does the Ministry intend to effectively enforce the regulations which are premised on giving a direction to the service provider and making non-compliance with such directions a criminal offence?

sections.label: Direction timeframe and enforcement
sections.summary: Asks whether the direction will state a timeframe, notes section 45G reverses burden of proof, and suggests user reporting and Gazette amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Will the timeframe be stated in the direction?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This is especially significant because the new section 45G reverses the burden of proof onto the electronic service provider to show that it had done the best that was reasonably practicable to do when it is charged with an offence under section 45E(1) or 45F(1).

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Perhaps we can consider enhancing a second prong of enforcement by relying on the user reporting avenues to flag objectionable content.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This may result in faster detection because we effectively rely on a wider pool of eyes to identify and flag "egregious content".

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While the Bill, if passed, starts off by targeting "social media services" only, the Minister will be authorised to amend or add to this list of services in the Fourth Schedule by publishing an order in the Gazette.

sections.label: Discord and online codes
sections.summary: Describes Discord as a gaming chat platform with over 140 million monthly active users, and notes section 45L prescribes consultation before online codes of practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is a gaming platform where gamers can chat, amongst others, within the Discord server.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: However, what is significant is that it has more than 140 million monthly active users now and it is being used beyond gaming.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, it is one example of an online communications service that has evolved and new things have come up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: These "regulated online communication services" may be subjected to one or more online codes of practice to be issued by IMDA, and the new section 45L states that the Minister will prescribe certain consultation processes to be followed before an online code of practice can be issued, amended or revoked.

sections.label: Child sexual exploitation content
sections.summary: States some researchers say such material is one quarter of daily search requests and seven in 10 children are exposed daily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: While statistics are hard to come by, some researchers indicate that it comprises one quarter of daily search engine requests and seven in 10 children are inadvertently exposed to such materials daily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I am glad that this Bill makes it clear that such content should not be exposed to our children, and child sexual exploitation in all its various forms on all platforms will be tackled aggressively.

sections.label: Missing take-down timeline
sections.summary: Notes the Bill does not stipulate a timeline, unlike Australia's 24-hour take-down window, and suggests applying the same.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The current proposed Bill does not stipulate a timeline, as many other Members have pointed out, compared to other countries, for example, in Australia, that indicate a 24-hour take-down window.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We should perhaps apply the same to our laws, so that the damage is limited and action can be taken so that harm to individuals can be avoided quickly in the light speed by which content travels in the metaverse today.

sections.label: Social media giant's new owner
sections.summary: Asks how the Ministry will proceed and handle a social media giant that may become unwilling to accept Singapore's rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As the company evolves to fit into their new owner's worldview, how will the Ministry take the process forward and how will we deal with potential difficulties of a social media giant which may well now become unwilling to accept the rules that we seek to enforce for the safety of Singaporean users?

sections.label: Pew survey on online safety
sections.summary: A Pew Research survey found 62% of teens and 50% of adults prefer a safe online environment over free speech online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In the most recent survey published by Pew Research in August 2022 on sentiments amongst teens and adults in that bastion of free speech, the US, 62% of teen respondents aged 13 to 17, who were surveyed, said that their top priority is a welcoming, safe online environment, and that is far more important than being able to speak their minds freely online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Even with the adults who were surveyed, while the results are more evenly spread, 50% as compared to 47%, they also prefer the same safe environment online.

sections.label: Metaverse policing and manpower
sections.summary: The Member foresees metaverse challenges for the Ministry and hopes it has enough manpower to enforce the Bill's safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I foresee the challenges that the changes to the metaverse would pose to society and to the Ministry in policing it and helping to keep all of us safe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I do hope that the Ministry will be able to muster sufficient manpower resources to quickly ensure that the safeguards spelt out in this Bill are as good in words as they are in action.

sections.label: Maximum fines under the Bill
sections.summary: Defaulting services may face fines up to $1 million under proposed sections 45E(1) and 45N, compared with the Privacy and Data Protection Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Next, on the legislative provisions in the Bill, under the proposed section 45E(1) where a service does not comply with blocking directions and the proposed section 45N which contemplates a situation where a prescribed service does not comply with the Code, the defaulting service may be liable to a maximum fine of up to $1 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: For comparison, under the Privacy and Data Protection Act, the maximum financial penalty was increased to the higher 10% of an organisation's annual turnover in Singapore or $1 million to send a stronger signal of Singapore's stance towards the importance of privacy and data protection.

sections.label: Question on increasing penalties
sections.summary: The Member asks whether the Ministry would consider increasing the maximum penalties under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry thus consider increasing the maximum penalties that can be meted out under the Bill?

sections.label: Overseas penalties and whole-of-society approach
sections.summary: The UK and Germany prescribe maximum fines, and success depends on a whole-of-society approach with community and industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In the United Kingdom, the Online Safety Bill currently prescribes a maximum fine of the higher of £18 million or 10% of the defaulting service's worldwide revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In Germany, the Network Enforcement Act prescribes a maximum penalty of up to €50 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The success of this goal will also be premised on contemplating a whole-of-society approach, where our efforts are to work closely with the community and industry stakeholders to equip Singaporeans with the knowledge and skills to keep themselves safe online.

sections.label: Updating laws and prioritising services
sections.summary: The Member says laws will be updated as needed, prioritising widely used services where safety risks are apparent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Like many Singaporeans we engaged, Members acknowledged the fast pace of change in the online landscape.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We are, therefore, committed to updating our laws and regulations as frequently as necessary to keep them relevant and effective.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In terms of the type of services, we will prioritise those that are more widely used in Singapore and where the safety risks have become or are becoming apparent.

sections.label: Designating entities in specified OCS
sections.summary: Which entities to designate within each specified OCS depends on their reach or impact with Singapore viewers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Within each specified OCS, which entities to designate will depend on how much reach or impact they have with Singapore viewers.

sections.label: Private communications with large memberships
sections.summary: Groups with very large memberships could propagate egregious content, making them no different from non-private communications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: While we do not intend to police private communications, we are also aware that there are groups with very large memberships, which could be used to propagate egregious content, making them no different from non-private communications.

sections.label: Loot boxes and Gambling Control Act
sections.summary: The Government recognises loot box harms and updated the Gambling Control Act to address in-game loot boxes monitored by the Gambling Regulatory Authority.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Government recognises the potential harms of loot boxes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This is why we made significant updates to the Gambling Control Act earlier this year to ensure that our laws are able to address emerging trends and products, such as in-game loot boxes, which are monitored by the Gambling Regulatory Authority.

sections.label: IMDA assessing harmful or egregious content
sections.summary: IMDA will objectively assess content harm considering context, and educational content helping users overcome harms will not be considered harmful or egregious.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: When assessing whether a piece of content is harmful or egregious, IMDA will take an objective approach, considering the context in which it is presented.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: If such content is educational in nature or helps users to overcome these harms, naturally, it will not be considered harmful or egregious.

sections.label: Bill purpose and freedom of speech
sections.summary: The Bill's overarching purpose is to provide a safe environment protecting online users while respecting freedom of speech and expression under Article 14.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: I would also like to remind Members of the overarching purpose of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: And that is, to provide a safe environment and conditions that protect online users, while respecting freedom of speech and expression, as enshrined in Article 14 of the Constitution.

sections.label: Financial penalty quantum comparison
sections.summary: The financial penalty quantum is comparable with other local legislation covering social media services, such as FICA and POFMA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The financial penalty quantum is comparable with other local legislation that covers social media services, such as the Foreign Interference (Countermeasures) Act and the Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act.

sections.label: IMDA blocking direction to providers
sections.summary: IMDA may issue a blocking direction to Internet Access Service Providers to stop Singapore users accessing these services if concerns remain unaddressed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In the event that these still fail to address our serious concerns, IMDA may then issue a blocking direction to Internet Access Service Providers to stop Singapore users from accessing these services.

sections.label: Section 45J(2) liability protection
sections.summary: Proposed section 45J(2) ensures compliance with IMDA directions does not cause a service provider to incur liability in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Mr Zhulkarnain also asked about the proposed section 45J(2).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This provision ensures that compliance with IMDA's directions does not cause a service provider to incur liability in Singapore, if, for example, the content creator takes issue with it.

sections.label: Reporting mechanisms for designated services
sections.summary: Under IMDA's draft Code of Practice for Online Safety, designated services must provide effective, transparent, easy-to-access and easy-to-use reporting mechanisms to all individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Under IMDA's draft Code of Practice for Online Safety, designated services will be required to provide effective, transparent, easy-to-access and easy-to-use reporting mechanisms to all individuals.

sections.label: Actions in annual reports
sections.summary: Services will be required to include information on these actions in their annual reports.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Services will be required to include information on these actions in their annual reports.

sections.label: Timeline for egregious content
sections.summary: For egregious content that could cause serious harm, the timeline would generally be within hours.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For egregious content that could cause serious harm, the timeline would, generally, be within hours.

sections.label: Differentiated accounts for children
sections.summary: The code requires services to provide differentiated accounts to children, with safety settings robust and set to more restrictive, age-appropriate levels by default.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The code also requires that services provide differentiated accounts to children, whereby safety settings are robust and set to more restrictive levels that are age-appropriate by default.

sections.label: Support centre for online harm victims
sections.summary: SHE is working with the Singapore Council of Women's Organisations to launch a support centre for victims of online harm.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Continuing the work of the Sunlight AFA, which concluded its tenure in July this year, SHE is working with the Singapore Council of Women's Organisations to launch a support centre for victims of online harm.

sections.label: MinLaw efforts on online harms
sections.summary: MinLaw is looking into empowering victims to stop online harms and hold those responsible accountable, complementing MCI and MHA efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: MinLaw is also looking into how victims can be better empowered to put a stop to such online harms generally, and to seek redress against and hold accountable those who are responsible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This includes cyberbullying and more novel forms of online hurt, such as cancel campaigns, which Minister Shanmugam has spoken about before.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: MinLaw's efforts will complement MCI's efforts to enhance the Government's regulatory tool kit, as well as MHA's efforts to address criminal offences committed online.

sections.label: Melvin Yong on self-regulatory task force
sections.summary: Mr Melvin Yong asked whether the Government would consider setting up a self-regulatory task force with key OCS providers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For example, Mr Melvin Yong asked whether the Government would consider setting up a self-regulatory task force with key OCS providers.

sections.label: Google online safety initiatives
sections.summary: Google held its Online Safety Park and is partnering the Media Literacy Council to train 50,000 parents and children on online safety.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To highlight a few examples, Google held its Online Safety Park at the Digital for Life Festival earlier this year and it is partnering the Media Literacy Council (MLC) to bring its "Be Internet Awesome" programme to Primary schools to train 50,000 parents and children on online safety measures.

sections.label: Meta anti-scam education campaigns
sections.summary: Meta collaborated with the National Crime Prevention Council and MLC on scam education campaigns reaching over two million users.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Meta collaborated with the National Crime Prevention Council and MLC on a campaign to educate users on top scam typologies and tips to keep safe.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This campaign reached over two million users and a second campaign has been launched on e-commerce scams.

sections.label: Bill for safer online environment
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to create a safer online environment, hold online services accountable, and let Government step in on egregious content.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Bill before us today seeks to create a safer online environment for Singapore users.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In turn, online services will be held accountable for their systems, processes and actions.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And where there is egregious content, such as content that undermines racial and religious harmony, the Government will step in to protect users.
